must_fix.where: R2.3 PC_PASS_1b; R.1 definitions of u_sea^perp* and u_T^perp*; R2.4 gating of 'unlikely'; R.0 and R.6
must_fix.problem: Under round-1/2 dynamics the redefined positive control is not passable at blocks 14 and 6. A failed control also turns the expected negative there into 'undecided'. Evidence from theta_verdict.json blocks.<b>.B_Q0.mode_set: SEA is a member of M_14 and M_6, so u*_14 and u*_6 contain the round-1 SEA loop's own d_4. The debiased cos(d_4^SEA, d_4^RSI_a) is -1.051 at 14 and -1.142 at 6, against 0.229 at 18. image_cos_d1_u_star.SEA is -0.930 / -0.834 / 0.118. u_sea^perp* is orthogonal to u*_b by construction, so a SEA loop with round-1 dynamics reads A of about 0 plus noise at n = 2-4 at 14 and 6. Even at d_1 at block 14, all of the non-u* residual would give at most sqrt(1-0.93^2)/sqrt(0.868) = 0.39. In addition, u*_6 is not a generic attractor: R4 says 'unaligned' and random_start_debiased_cos.RND_1 is 0.0099. Projecting it out of u_T and u_sea at block 6 therefore removes the persistent direction that the RSI and SEA loops share there, not style. Expected outcome: PC_PASS_1b only at block 18; at 14 and 6, 'undecided (positive control failed)' exactly where the RSI A on u_T^perp* would be tightly near 0; the delta rule again 'not decidable'.
must_fix.fix: (a) Gate negative verdicts on a measurement-sensitivity check instead of PC_PASS_1b. SENS_1b(b): plant A = 0.25 (kappa unit(axis)) into the 1b DN rows 2-4 of RND_1/RND_2 (or into the RSI rows after centring them on the axis). Read through the full pipeline on u_T^perp* and u_sea^perp* (cross-fit, joint bootstrap, K1-s; R0.7's method), 500 replicates. Pass if p_s <= 0.01 and A_lo >= 0.10 at all three rows in >= 80 % of replicates. 'unlikely (RSI does not persist)' and 'unlikely (no first link)' then require SENS_1b, not PC_PASS_1b. Keep PC_PASS_1b required for 'likely' and 'oscillation', and report it as a substantive outcome, with the label 'no topic persists beyond the generic mode at b' when SEA_t and SPO_t both have A upper bounds < 0.25 at n = 3 and 4. (b) Project u*_b out only at blocks where round 2 found an RND-attracted mode (blocks 14 and 18). At block 6 use u_T_perp^1b and u_sea_perp (sea minus span(u_T, sports, tone, u_neg)) together with the P5 RND contrast. (c) State this expectation, with the numbers above, in R2.3 and R.0.

must_fix.where: R1 Rule (reproduction flag) and the R2.6 ladder rung L2
must_fix.problem: 'Replay reproduces round 1' cannot be reached in the closed-loop rounds, even with byte-identical code. Round-0 texts diverge at about 3-6 % per text (L4 to A100; G47 match rates 0.969 / 0.938). That re-samples about 8-15 of 128 pairs after their divergence point and turns d_1 by roughly 5-15 %. The pushes along d_1..d_3 then shift logits by orders of magnitude more than float noise, so most texts of evaluations 1-3 diverge. Criterion (i) (>= 0.85 token-identical per evaluation) therefore fails at rounds >= 1. Criterion (ii) (|dc| and |drel| <= 0.05 for every row) fails by chance: SD(c) at 64x2 is 0.029 / 0.050 / 0.044, so across 48 rows a breach is near certain at blocks 18 and 6. The flag would read 'replay differs' for reasons that have nothing to do with reproducibility.
must_fix.fix: Apply (i) only to evaluations whose push is a stored round-1 vector (pilots and round 0). Add an open-loop replay of rounds 1-3: rk.evaluate(L+SUF, n, d=R1.state[b]['dir_<L><SUF>_<n>'], nseed, alpha), with round-1 keys and the same byte-identical function, and apply (i) per evaluation to it. This adds 6,144 texts, about 6.5 A100-min with margin. Replace (ii) by a paired tolerance on the open-loop rows: |dc| and |drel| <= 2.5 x the prompt-bootstrap SD of the replay-minus-round-1 difference. Report the closed-loop token identity per round descriptively, as rung L2. Condition the expected identity on GPU, torch and CUDA versions, not on the GPU name alone.

must_fix.where: R4.2 lambda_max / lambda_S rules; R4.3 lambda_direct
must_fix.problem: (a) lambda_max comes from power iteration, which keeps the largest |Rayleigh quotient| (largest modulus; possibly negative or complex), while lambda_S is defined as 'the largest real eigenvalue' of Q'JQ. The rules compare the two, which is meaningless for a negative or complex top mode, and 'largest real eigenvalue' is undefined when all four eigenvalues are complex. (b) lambda_max is cross-fitted, but lambda_RSI is the in-sample maximum over 4 noisy eigenvalues and so biased upward. This biases lambda_max^cf - lambda_RSI toward 'RSI is the top mode', and 'near critical' / '>= 1' toward passing. (c) The denominators w_A'v_A and w.v are unguarded; for non-normal J they approach 0, and the mean over halvings is then dominated by outliers. (d) There is no null for lambda_max^cf. J is 2048x2048, estimated from 1,920 half-sample texts with strongly anisotropic noise (B-Q7 per-text product SD 4.3 along u* against 0.30 along ('cov',14,4)), so the top pair of J_A can be a noise pair. The MDEs (0.098 / 0.134) assume fixed-direction SDs.
must_fix.fix: Define both quantities as the eigenvalue with the largest real part (report modulus and phase), computed the same way. Use Arnoldi with forward products only (k = 20) on J_A and take the Ritz value with the largest real part; for lambda_S use the 4x4 problem on the A half. Take the held-out value z'J_B y/(z'y) for both, and the median over 20 halvings x 2 instead of the mean. Guard: if |cos(v_A, w_A)| < 0.2, use v_A'J_B v_A and label 'non-normal: Rayleigh read'; same in R4.3. Add a permutation null: 20 runs with S rows permuted across texts within prompt, so E[J] = 0. 'lambda_max resolved' only if lambda_max^cf exceeds the null's 95th percentile; otherwise every R4.2 and R4.3 verdict is 'not decidable (top mode not resolved)'. Re-derive the MDEs by a planted-spike simulation at TXT0 noise.

must_fix.where: R.5 order; R4.2 / R4.3 / R5.5 'Runs in'; RG14 / R7.3
must_fix.problem: R4.3 runs in R-S3 and needs v_max and v_RSI (Inputs: R4.2), but R4.2's eigen-analysis is placed in R-Sana, which comes after wave 3. R5.5 (R-S5, wave 3) also needs R4.2's v_max. RG14 is 'decided in R-S7' but needs V_RSI_1b(14), which exists only after R-Sana pass 1, i.e. after R-S7.
must_fix.fix: Run the full-sample eigen-analysis at the end of each R-S3 block process, before R4.3: Arnoldi or power iteration on the in-session X and S, plus the 4x4 restricted problems; seconds of GPU time. Store v_max, w_max, v_S and w_S per block. Keep the cross-fit, nulls and bootstrap in R-Sana. For R7.3, either define RG14 with in-session data only (the twin's first round from s0: p_s <= 0.01 and A_lo >= 0.10), or move R7.3 into a conditional session after R-Sana pass 1 (about 4.6 work x 1.5 + 4 setup + 1.5 copy-in, about 13 A100-min) and update the 'decided in' column.

must_fix.where: R2.3 and R2.4 MDE paragraphs; R.1 Statistics
must_fix.problem: The MDEs are given per component, not for the rules as used. (a) P1 needs three rows jointly. A normal-model simulation with rows correlated 0.5-0.8 gives a joint MDE80 of about 0.23-0.24 at block 14 (SD_A 0.045) and 0.19-0.20 at 18 and 6 (SD_A 0.033), against the stated 0.21 / 0.18. P2-P5 multiply on top. P4's power is unknown at the freeze: its SD is measured only in R0.6, after the freeze, and it consists of three separate p <= 0.01 tests. (b) SD(A_bar) assumes RSI_a and RSI_b are independent, but they share all 256 prompts (between-prompt share of per-pair noise about 0.46). With a between-loop correlation of 0.5, SD(A_bar) is about 0.038 at block 14 (not 0.028-0.032); power for 'substantial' at the stated MDE A_bar = 0.33 is about 0.68, and the real MDE is about 0.35. (c) 'SD(E) about 0.05' holds only for A >= 0.5 with high round-to-round correlation; at A = 0.25-0.33 at block 14, SD(E) is about 0.06-0.13.
must_fix.fix: Pre-register joint MDEs by simulating the full verdict functions (PC_PASS_1b and every R2.4 string) under a stated noise model: SD_A per block from mde_R, within-loop correlation 0.5-0.8, between-loop correlation 0.5. Calibrate that model in R0 on the R1 replay and round-1 RSI_a/RSI_b with the joint bootstrap. Replace P4's three tests by one pooled sign-flip test over evaluations 1-3 at 0.01, and publish its MDE (words per text pair) from R0.6 before R2's analysis. State SD(E) per block and per A level.

must_fix.problem: R.6 counts any of about 15 outcomes as 'for' the hypothesis: 'likely' at 3 blocks; 'reaches 1' along u_T^perp* at 3 blocks; 'lambda_RSI >= 1' or 'near critical' plus 'top mode' at 3 blocks; K 'self-sustaining' at 2 temperatures x K_2 and K_geo; C-Q4b 'survives' or 're-routed'. Each uses roughly a 5 % one-sided level, and the union has no family-wise control, so a 'for' reading is likely under the global null. Across blocks only p_s is Bonferroni-adjusted; the 90 % margin bounds that decide the A tiers are not.
must_fix.fix: Define one confirmatory 'for' family, for example: V_RSI_1b 'likely' at each decidable block; R3.3 'reaches 1' along u_T^perp*; R4.2 'lambda_RSI >= 1'; R6.2 K_2 'self-sustaining' at T 0.7. Apply Holm at family-wise 0.05 to it, with margin bounds at the adjusted level (1 - 0.10/k intervals). Label everything else exploratory. Print the counts of 'for' and 'against' outcomes next to their expected counts under the null.

must_fix.where: R6.3, R6.1, R2.4 (E), R3.3, R4.2, R2.4 precedence
must_fix.problem: Several verdict strings and 'not decidable' conditions are missing. R6.3 has no string for K's lower bound > 1. R6.1's rho = g_soft/g_text has no 'not decidable' case, although along u_T^perp* g_text is about 0.02-0.05 with SD about 0.025, so its interval will contain 0. E has no denominator condition. R3.3's 'best of three cells' is wrong when the DN cell is <= 0.5 alpha_0 (along u*_14 it sits at 0.34-0.36 alpha_0, giving 4 cells). R4.2's 'largest real eigenvalue' is undefined for a complex spectrum. No precedence is given when GO0_1b, RG7/RG8, RG9 and RG5 outcomes coincide; round 1 used an if/elif chain (rk_verdict.py:91-98).
must_fix.fix: Add 'replicated, self-sustaining (K lower bound > 1)' to R6.3. In R6.1, define rho only if g_text's 90 % interval excludes 0; otherwise 'not decidable (text gain not resolved)' (code NaN:denominator_interval_includes_0). Define E only if the interval of A_2^a + A_2^b excludes 0; otherwise 'likely' and 'oscillation' are unreachable and E is reported as the code. Set k = the number of cells with a <= 0.5 alpha_0, the DN cell included. Handle complex spectra as in MF3. Fix the precedence: label 'descriptive (code check failed)' > 'not decidable (RSI axis not resolved)' > 'not decidable (damage calibration failed)' > 'undecided (positive control not testable)' > 'undecided (positive control failed)' (or SENS failed, per MF1) > likely-dominated > likely-substantial > oscillation > unlikely (does not persist) > unlikely (no first link) > undecided.

must_fix.where: R0.5 / R0.6 (PC_PASS_R0 on u_sea^perp*, the block-6 'style-confounded' label, SEA minus RND); R2.6 rungs L0-L2 read on u_T^perp*
must_fix.problem: Readings of round-1 and replay loops on the perp* axes use round 2's u*_b, which was built from those same loops' d_4. The mode sets are M_14 = RSI_a, RSI_b, SEA, SPO, RND_1; M_18 = RSI_a, RND_1, r2RSIb; M_6 = RSI_a, SEA, r2RSIb (r2_theta.py:220-224). The A of SEA on u_sea^perp*, and of RSI_a/RSI_b on u_T^perp*, is then partly suppressed by construction. That makes PC_PASS_R0 on u_sea^perp*, the block-6 'style-confounded' label and the ladder's A_n at L0-L2 partly predetermined.
must_fix.fix: For every reading of round-1 or replay data on a perp* axis, use a leave-loop-out mode: u*_b^(-L) = unit(sum over M_b without L and its twin of sg_L' d_4^L'); for RSI_a also drop RSI_b and r2RSIb. Say so where nothing or only RND_1 remains (block 18). Report the full-u* reading beside it, labelled 'self-overlapping'.

must_fix.problem: RG3 compares against 'the round-1 values recorded by round 2's G3', but those values do not exist for this set. Round 2's G3 hashed R1_MODULES = rk_loop.py, pc_meta.py, pc_common.py, ufo_common.py, rsi_statements.py (r2_run_session.py:206, 847-880): rk_verdict.py is not among them. round2_summary.json gates.G3 stores only {name, labels}, no hashes. must_fix.fix: Freeze the constants in the plan. They are identical at HEAD c8257c2 and at the round-1 gpu1 commit 740bfc0f: rk_loop.py 1a20f61992637386c97197b7283a8b743214aa89028f504c4af6c2fbedbab2a1; rk_verdict.py 62aced20fcd7435201e1f427e5c294869fdab3adcb54801f092aa8d31ab9049e; ufo_common.py 6f3919e93b638a325f9a8dd5762430c6b5e7693d4e1f5a317d97366caa49f9ab; rsi_statements.py 6ff560c5b9c092858c7b50c4b041b7c886329bb7a451a6738d6eaa3754e3bec2. Also check them with git at every round-1 shard's code_commit, as gate_G3 does.

must_fix.where: R.5 session table and budget argument; R2.2 / R3.3 storage lists
must_fix.problem: The cost arithmetic reproduces (cost_R.py: 597 min; 8.06 h unconditional; 11.58 / 13.62 h at half generation speed), but four items are missing or wrong. (a) R-Sana copy-in assumes 2.5 GB, which matches float32 storage of the 'all' window only. R2.2 and R3.3 store all three read windows, and read_windows returns float64: 5.9 GB in float32 or 11.8 GB in float64, i.e. 59 or 117 min at the spec's own 10 min/GB, not 25. (b) R-Sana passes 1 and 2 are separated by R-S5b and R-S8, so pass 2 is a second session (+3 min setup + copy-in). (c) Drive writes are not costed: about 1.1 GB per R-S2 session and about 1.7 GB from R-S3. (d) R1 counts 384 texts too many at blocks 18 and 6 (the pilot evaluations are the loops' round 0). Net change is about +1.9 h: about 10.0 h unconditional and 11.9 h with both conditional sessions at planned rates. At half generation speed, after the pre-registered reductions, it is about 14 h, not 'near 12 h'.
must_fix.fix: Specify storage: float32; the 'all' window as full vectors; 'div' and 'first20' only as projections onto the <= 12 fixed axes the rules read. That gives about 2.6 GB in total. Cost R-Sana as two sessions. Cost Drive writes per session at the placeholder rate. Add a second pre-registered reduction tier that triggers at >= 2.0 s per generate call: NP arm at block 14 only; R6.1 iterated loops dropped; R5.2 and R5.3 nulls cut from 20 to 10.

should_fix: R1 opener: run the replay stages as subprocesses, exactly as run_shard.rk does (run_shard.py:64-72): `python rk_loop.py <root> <work>/r1b_replay/rk <stage>` with env BLOCK, ASCALE, POOLDIRS and PERSONA. Importing with argv 'lib' needs rk.stage to be reassigned before rk.main(), which is not the round-1 code path.
r2_rk.stats_on_axis (r2_rk.py:563) falls back to rk.NP = 64 whenever a block is open. Every r1b call must pass n_prompts=256 (and use halvings(256)), otherwise rel is computed on the wrong halvings.

AX-1b reuses round-1 axis texts for the 64 old prompts. Those texts were generated per block on different GPUs (gpu1 on an L4), so the text set differs between blocks, and R7.1's CRN pairs mix L4-generated references with A100-generated ablated texts. Regenerate these 512 texts once in R-S2/14 with their round-1 keys (16 generate calls) and use that one set at every block.

Fold-axis attenuation (about 0.97) makes the upper-bound rules slightly anti-conservative ('unlikely', 'no first link', SPO_t's bound, R3.3 'below 1'); it does not only make lower-bound rules conservative. Disattenuate by the cross-fold axis cosine, or say so.

R4.1: with 15 seeds per prompt, centre x within prompt (correct by n_s/(n_s-1)). This removes between-prompt variance, and RSI-topic and scene prompts differ along the RSI axes. For blocks 18 and 6 use their own B-Q7 SDs (u_T_perp 0.166 / 0.153; u* 0.110 / 0.169; sea 0.205 / 0.112), not block 14's.

R6.2: read D_k on the cross-fitted fold axes, as every other 1b readout does. Add a random-direction carry control (DN RND_1 start pushed at a_DN, turns 2-3) so that RSI carry can be compared with generic carry.

R5.3: 'specific in use' requires every foreign set's interval to contain 0. Teacher-forced shifts are deterministic per text and any push moves every word set a little, so this is practically unreachable. Compare the foreign sets with the null directions' 5-95 % range, as is done for the neutral sets.

R5.4: dim_batch 128 replicates a prompt of about 150 tokens 128 times, which needs about 40 GB of bf16 activations. On an A100-40GB use dim_batch <= 64 (total backward FLOPs are unchanged per the jlens docstring), or require the 80-GB card.
R5.1 at blocks 2, 10, 22, 24 and 26: u_sea_perp^1b needs u_neg at those blocks. Add the 80 NEG sentences to the all-block read.
R5.5: label-shuffled null axes (pro/anti swapped per prompt) are uncentred sign-flip nulls (E.diff/N), the very construction 1b replaces. Use centred pseudo-axes.
R2.7: 'generic attractor' tests an RND loop against u*_1b, which includes that same loop when it is in the mode set (the self-overlap int_gates flagged). Use a leave-one-out u*_1b.

R3.3: specify diagonal WLS weights and bootstrap the whole fit. A GLS on the bootstrap covariance of key-sharing cells would invert a near-singular matrix. Also reword R.1's 'no matrix inversion anywhere': WLS and K_geo solve 2x2 normal equations, which the rule allows as a regression fit, since no inverse is used for reconstruction.

Give the R3.3 MDE for blocks 18 and 6. The pre-registered reductions drop the 0.35 alpha_0 cell at 18 and 6, so k becomes 2 there; state this conditional k, and note that these reductions are not 'descriptive only'.
R0.7's nested bootstrap for rule M costs about 6e14 FLOP: run it on the A100, not on the CPU, or use 200 inner replicates.
List in R.7 that the E rule changed (round 1: point E >= 0.7; 1b: lower bound >= 0.5). State whether R_4^cf >= 0.5, mean rel >= 0.5 and D4 > 0 are point conditions or bound conditions.
Freeze the neutral word pool (the list and its sha256) in the plan; at present it is only described.
Waves 1 and 3 each run three concurrent sessions in account A, while round 2 assumed at most 2 per account (int_machinery). Stagger them or move R-S5 to account B.
R8.2: the 0.6B PC axis keeps the style mode, since no u* exists for 0.6B. Label that PC 'not style-free'.
R0's README-null rule has no string for rows that move the other way (p <= 0.01 to p_c > 0.01). Report the counts in both directions.
check.budget_check:
Re-derived with the spec's own cost_R.py and slow_R.py (taskset -c 3 python3 -I, no model). The result matches the spec: 597.0 A100-min total = 9.95 h, of which 8.06 h unconditional, at the round-2 planned rates (P2 7.1, lines 1375-1403).

Independent spot checks also match:
- R2.2: 4,864 pairs per round, about 32.8 / 34.4 min of work per block.
- R3.3: 50,688 texts, about 34.9 min.
- R1 block 14: 4,480 texts.
- R6.2: 11,264 texts at 2.0 s.

At half generation speed the totals are 11.58 h unconditional and 13.62 h overall. The pre-registered reductions save about 1.5 h (re-derived):
- RSI rounds 5-6: 22 min
- FX arm at 18 and 6: 15 min
- R3.3 doses at 18 and 6: 15 min
- R6.1 iterated loops: 23 min
- R5.4 on 200 texts: about 15 min

Omissions (+ about 1.9 h at the spec's own 10 min/GB placeholder):
- R-Sana copy-in: 5.9 GB in float32 (11.8 GB in float64) with three read windows, against the 2.5 GB budgeted: +34 min or more.
- A second R-Sana session for pass 2: +28 min.
- Drive writes from R-S2 and R-S3 (about 4.6 GB): +about 50 min.
- DN calibrations in R3.3: +0.5 min.
- R1 overcount of 384 texts at blocks 18 and 6: -1 min.

Corrected totals: about 10.0 h unconditional and 11.9 h with both conditional sessions at planned rates, within the roughly 12-h envelope. At half generation speed after the reductions it is about 14 h, above the envelope. The 10 min/GB placeholder dominates the overrun, so R-P's Drive throughput measurement decides whether this matters.

All sessions stay below the 5-h limit; the largest is R-S5b at 95 min.
check.summary:
The spec is detailed and mostly consistent with the code. Cited functions and line ranges check out: open_block, the state guard, RefKL, calibrate, ConstPush, CbarHook, read_windows, fixed_fold_axes, prompt_bootstrap and score_grads/lambda_lin. The quoted round-2 numbers match theta_verdict.json: med 189.06 / 514.76 / 59.47, alpha_b, g_par of the RND starts, the B-Q7 SDs and the R1 points. The MDE scripts reproduce. The inverse-free rule is respected; only the claim 'no matrix inversion anywhere' is overstated, since WLS fits solve normal equations. Nothing produces analysable data before the freeze.

Six main problems:
1. The repaired positive control is very likely unpassable at blocks 14 and 6. SEA is in round 2's mode set there (debiased cos(d_4^SEA, d_4^RSI_a) = -1.05 / -1.14), and u*_6 is not a generic attractor (RND_1 0.0099). A failed control then blocks exactly the negative RSI verdicts that 1b could reach. Fix: gate negatives on a planted-signal sensitivity check, and project u* out only at blocks with an RND-attracted mode.
2. The replay's reproduction rule fails by construction in the closed-loop rounds. Fix: an open-loop replay that pushes along round 1's stored d_n.
3. The R4.2 eigen definitions and estimators are inconsistent and biased: largest modulus against largest real part, an in-sample max against a cross-fitted value, unguarded w'v denominators, no noise null.
4. The session order contradicts itself: R4.3 and R5.5 need eigenvectors that are computed later, and RG14 needs V_RSI_1b before R-Sana has run.
5. Statistics: MDEs are per component, not for the conjunctive rules; RSI_a and RSI_b are treated as independent although they share prompts; the 'for' family has no multiplicity control; several 'not decidable' strings and the verdict precedence are missing; R0 has self-overlap; RG3's reference hashes do not exist as described.
6. Copy-in and Drive-write costs are underestimated by about 1.9 h.

Check scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DSSE/85db304a-b0fa-5d03-b685-f9acf8fac842/scratchpad/r1b/chk_R/joint_power.py, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DSSE/85db304a-b0fa-5d03-b685-f9acf8fac842/scratchpad/r1b/chk_R/e_sd.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DSSE/85db304a-b0fa-5d03-b685-f9acf8fac842/scratchpad/r1b/chk_R/volume.py.

measurements.what: Declared engineering pilot before the freeze: generate / read / forward-backward / soft-generation / RefKL rates, peak memory, Drive read and write throughput, replay openers on MOCK; throwaway prompts, no analysable data; its rates fix the reduction tier (RG18)

Model-free re-analysis of round-1 raw files: reproduction, centred pseudo-axes, cross-fitted disattenuated paired sign-flip test, cross-fitted S_4/R_4, gate re-evaluation on raw u_sea and the verdict sea axis with leave-loop-out modes (post hoc; only block 6 can reopen), topic specificity and the PC expectation, size and power plants (200 inner replicates, A100 runtime), calibration of the joint power model

Round-1-identical replay as round 1 ran it: byte-identical rk_loop.py stages as subprocesses (run_shard path) on reduced state copies, same prompts, axes, alpha, cap, starts and Gumbel keys (4,480 / 2,048 / 2,432 texts at 14 / 18 / 6); token identity per round descriptive (rung L2)

Open-loop replay: rk.evaluate along round 1's stored dir_<L><SUF>_n (n = 1-3) with round-1 keys in a separate state copy, 6,144 texts; reproduction flag (version-conditioned token identity, paired tolerance on c and rel, gate list and open-loop PC_PASS)

P256 prompts and AX-1b axes (one A100-generated axis text set incl. the 64 round-1 prompts regenerated with round-1 keys; verdict axes u_X^v = perp* at 14); loops in DN (primary), FX (attribution) and NP (control) arms, 512/256 pairs, 4 rounds (+2 for RSI)
AX-1b reads (verdict axes = perp* at 18) and the three-arm loops at block 18
AX-1b reads (verdict axes = ^1b at 6, because u*_6 is not a generic mode) and the three-arm loops at block 6
